# Shape: rows are not the only axis

<!-- Generated by `cargo xtask bench-shapes` from crates/engine/examples/bench_shapes.rs. Don't edit by hand. -->

> **Generated** for Cella 0.13.0 at `fee5e04` (2026-11-26). Machine: windows x86_64. The same commands at three workbook shapes, each with the same number of cells.

Every other ruler here varies **rows**. This one holds the cell count at 8,000,000 and moves them around: the same eight million cells as a million-row sheet, as a thousand-column sheet, and as a hundred sheets of ten thousand rows. A command that is O(columns) or O(sheets) has no way to show it in a row count, and a row-only ruler reports such a command as fast.

| shape | rows | columns | sheets | what it is |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---|
| `tall` | 1,000,000 | 8 | 1 | a million rows, eight columns |
| `wide` | 8,000 | 1,000 | 1 | a thousand columns, eight thousand rows |
| `sheets` | 10,000 | 8 | 100 | a hundred sheets of ten thousand rows |

A cell is the command's own wall clock, run alone in a fresh session holding a copy of that shape, with its region-naming params over the whole used area — the same generator the command catalogue uses.

Two things to read with care. **A command that works on one sheet sees only the active sheet's cells in the `sheets` shape** (10,000 × 8 = 80,000 of the eight million), so its `sheets` cell is a smaller job, not the same one; `file.saveBytes` and `sheet.rename` are the rows whose axis really is the sheet count. And **`home.formatCells` refuses a rectangle over 4,000,000 cells that is neither whole rows nor whole columns** (`crates/engine/src/cmd/format.rs`, measured there: 0.4 s at 4M, 0.82 s at 8M, 1.52 s at 16M), so its two big shapes show that refusal instead of a number; a whole row or column takes the line-style path.

| command | what it does | tall | wide | sheets |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `edit.find` | scans every used cell | 196 us | 71 us | 38 us |
| `edit.clearFormats` | walks every cell's style | 158 ms | 35 ms | 1.0 ms |
| `home.formatCells` | writes a style per cell | (params: selection too large to f…) | (params: selection too large to f…) | 16 ms |
| `edit.clearAll` | clears the used area | 8.3 ms | 1.4 ms | 3.1 ms |
| `data.sortAscending` | sorts the body by one column | 1.16 s | 789 ms | 15 ms |
| `range.move` | moves a block | 1.26 s | 1.03 s | 22 ms |
| `home.autofitColumnWidth` | measures every column | 180 ms | 1.9 ms | 6.6 ms |
| `file.saveBytes` | serialises the workbook | 1.62 s | 806 ms | 1.25 s |
| `home.conditionalFormat` | a conditional-format rule over the area | 817 us | 46 us | 111 us |
| `data.filter` | an AutoFilter over the area | 917 us | 42 us | 94 us |
| `edit.copy` | copies the area | 9.4 ms | 521 ms | 23 ms |
| `sheet.rename` | per-sheet work (should follow sheets, not cells) | 6.4 ms | 76 us | 6.8 ms |

## Where the shape changes the answer

Same cells, same command, a different arrangement — and more than four times apart. A row whose `sheets` cell is one percent of the cells (`data.sortAscending`, `edit.clearAll`, `edit.clearFormats`, `edit.find`) is a spread between the tall and wide columns, not across all three:

| command | fastest shape | slowest shape | times |
|---|---|---|---:|
| `edit.clearFormats` | sheets (1.0 ms) | tall (158 ms) | **152×** |
| `home.autofitColumnWidth` | wide (1.9 ms) | tall (180 ms) | **93×** |
| `sheet.rename` | wide (76 us) | sheets (6.8 ms) | **90×** |
| `data.sortAscending` | sheets (15 ms) | tall (1.16 s) | **77×** |
| `range.move` | sheets (22 ms) | tall (1.26 s) | **57×** |
| `edit.copy` | tall (9.4 ms) | wide (521 ms) | **56×** |
| `data.filter` | wide (42 us) | tall (917 us) | **22×** |
| `home.conditionalFormat` | wide (46 us) | tall (817 us) | **18×** |
| `edit.clearAll` | wide (1.4 ms) | tall (8.3 ms) | **6×** |
| `edit.find` | sheets (38 us) | tall (196 us) | **5×** |
